# TechDraw and Shop Drawings

TechDraw is FreeCAD's 2D documentation workbench. It projects the 3D model onto
a page, adds dimensions and annotations, and exports a PDF, SVG, or DXF. This is
the part of FreeCAD that replaces the screenshots-and-sections workflow from the
SolidCraft track.

## What you will learn

- How to create a TechDraw page and place views.
- How to add projected, section, and detail views.
- How to dimension and annotate a drawing.
- How to export a drawing for the shop.

## The drawing workflow

A reliable sequence:

1. Finish and check the 3D model.
2. Create a TechDraw page with a template and a title block.
3. Insert a view of the Body or assembly.
4. Add projected views (front, top, side).
5. Add a section or detail view for the joint that matters.
6. Add dimensions and annotations.
7. Check the scale, line weights, and title block.
8. Export PDF for printing and DXF/SVG if the shop needs it.

TechDraw is not a freehand 2D drafting program. It projects the model. If a
dimension is wrong, fix the model, not the drawing.

## Pages, templates, and views

A page uses a template, usually A4 or A3, with a title block. You can use the
default templates or make your own with your shop's name and revision fields.

Useful view types:

- **Insert View** — a single view of a selected object.
- **Projection Group** — front/top/side views in one step.
- **Section View** — cuts the model and shows the inside.
- **Detail View** — enlarges a small area.
- **BIM DrawingView** — in FreeCAD 1.1, creates plan/elevation drawings from
  BIM objects for use on a TechDraw page.

For a fence panel, the useful set is a plan, a front elevation, and a section
through a rail-to-post connection. For a deck, a framing plan and a stair
section. For a shed, a floor plan, wall elevation, and roof section.

## Dimensions and annotations

TechDraw dimensions are linked to the projected geometry. Add:

- overall length, width, and height;
- post spacing and joist spacing;
- rail and picket positions;
- hole diameters and edge distances;
- notes for material, fasteners, and finish.

Keep dimensions off the part outline where possible. A drawing that is crowded
with dimensions is harder to read than one with a clean overall view and a
detailed section.

## Build along: a fence panel drawing

1. Open the fence panel from Chapter 20.
2. Create a TechDraw page with an A3 template and title block.
3. Insert a front elevation and a plan view.
4. Add a section through a rail-to-post connection.
5. Dimension the overall height, bay width, post spacing, and picket gap.
6. Add notes for material and fasteners.
7. Export `drawings/20-fence-panel.pdf`.
8. Export a DXF copy if you want to edit the layout in another 2D tool.

## Checks

- The page uses the intended template and scale.
- Every important dimension appears once, not twice.
- Section and detail views show the joint clearly.
- The title block has the project name, date, and revision.
- The PDF opens and prints at the correct size.
- The DXF/SVG export preserves the line work.

## Exercises

1. Make a three-view drawing of the notched post from Chapter 17.
2. Add a section through a half-lap joint and dimension the lap depth.
3. Create a deck stair elevation with rise and run dimensions.
4. Make a shed wall elevation with the door opening and stud spacing.
5. Export the same page as PDF and DXF. Compare what survives.
